title: The Wording Effect: Quantifying Two-Way Drift in LLM Benchmark Performance
abstract: arXiv:2608.11694v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A benchmark score comes from a single phrasing of each problem. That single phrasing is treated as if it stood for the whole space of ways the same problem could be asked, but it does not. We show that rephrasing a problem while keeping its meaning and answer fixed routinely flips a model's answer in both directions, so some failures become successes and some successes become failures. We call this drift. BenchDrift generates meaning-preserving variations of benchmark problems along four axes, namely linguistic, referential, pragmatic, and structural, and measures how often, and why, correctness flips under each. Across eight models and three benchmarks (GSM8K, MMLU, MATH-Hard), we observe that drift is large in both directions. Two findings stand out. First, phrasing sensitivity does not fade as models get better. Instead, it changes sign. Weak models gain more from rephrasing than they lose, while strong models lose far more than the

translated_title: 措辞效应：量化大型语言模型基准性能中的双向漂移
translated_abstract: 基准分数来自每个问题的单一措辞。这种单一措辞被当作代表了同一问题可能被提出的所有方式的空间，但实际上并非如此。我们表明，在保持问题含义和答案不变的情况下重新措辞，通常会双向翻转模型的答案，因此一些失败变成成功，一些成功变成失败。我们称这种为漂移。BenchDrift沿着四个维度（即语言、指称、语用和结构）生成基准问题的意义保持变体，并测量在每个维度下正确性翻转的频率和原因。在八个模型和三个基准（GSM8K、MMLU、MATH-Hard）中，我们观察到漂移在两个方向上都很显著。有两个发现尤为突出。首先，措辞敏感性并不会随着模型变得更好而消失。相反，它会改变符号。弱模型从重新措辞中获得的比失去的多，而强模型失去的远多于获得的。
tldr: 本研究揭示了基准测试中措辞变化导致的性能双向漂移现象，并发现模型越强，措辞敏感性反而导致更多正确到错误的翻转。
en_tdlr: This study reveals bidirectional performance drift in benchmarks caused by wording variations, and finds that stronger models suffer more correct-to-incorrect flips due to phrasing sensitivity.
